D1 uses the existing envelope/verifier to satisfy R3-R5 without a second proof format. D2 preserves authority scope. Reviewed path, link, rotation, listing and FIFO corrections enforce R1/R7; sealed structural observation reports no additional material delta.

CLI help and docs describe init/pin/list/rotate, signing and authority flags, external coexistence and explicit trust. Paths and permission errors match the implementation; all five prior regression cases are covered.

Invalid names, permissions, project-local directories, linked files and special files fail with actionable errors. Pin and rotation require apply; rotations preserve archives and report the new pin. Fresh-instance signing journey passes.

R1-R7 and the five fixes were independently inspected; no unrelated runtime changes are attributed. Reviewer agent:independent-gpt-6.1-sol-review uses the prefix required by the engine under declared identity, as authorized by the maintainer until run-provenance replaces it. This review is by another vendor: OpenAI Codex versus implementer Anthropic Claude Opus 5.5 (agent:claude-opus-5-5); the prefix is a declaration, not authenticated run provenance.

Private seed remains only in the external key file; output and serialization exclude it. Loading rejects symlinks, extra Unix hard links, nonregular files and broad permissions. Trust requires an explicit public-key pin; unpinned envelopes and unauthorized human claims fail. Native signing does not bypass preflight. Cheapest fake independence is a typed prefix under declared assurance: adversarial corpus declared-independent-prefix prevents presenting that as authenticated separation; this attestation discloses it.

A native signer around the existing verifier is the smallest sufficient alternative to the external-only issuer. No new envelope, network service or hosted key manager. The design would need revisiting if passphrase/hardware protection became required.
